To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for base-stock inventory–queues, inter-departure time distributions are generally not exponentially distributed, but rather are mixtures of Erlang distributions, and that the squared coefficient of variation is generally greater than one.
the inter-departure time in an inventory-queue with a birth–death production process is an exponential distribution if the base-stock level is infinite or if the production rate is constant.

the inter-departure time distributions of the base-stock inventory-queue with birth–death processes are a mixture of Erlang and hyperexponential distributions and that the squared coefficients of variation of inter-departures are always larger than one.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three problems: (i) the analysis of inventory-queues; (ii) the characterization of the inter-departure time distribution in inventory-queues and (iii) the analysis of inter-departures times in inventory-queues.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the squared coefficient of variation of an inter-departure time in a base-stock inventory-queue is equal to the squared coefficient of variations for a corresponding standard queue if and only if the production process is Poisson.

for the base-stock inventory-queue the inter-departure time distribution is a mixture of two Erlang distributions, one of them is the inter-arrival time distribution of the input flow and the other one is the inter-arrivals time distribution of the service times.

for the base-stock inventory-queue with a Poisson job arrival stream, a birth–death production process, and a finite capacity buffer, the inter-departure time distribution is a mixture of two Erlang distributions, one with a squared coefficient of variation less than one and another with a squared coefficient greater than one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inter-departure time distribution is a mixture of a deterministic and an exponential distribution, and that the squared coefficient of variation of the inter-departures is always less than one.
we provide a detailed analysis of the inter-departure time process for a large class of inventory-queue models.

the squared coefficient of variation of the inter-departure time in an inventory-queue with base-stock control is equal to the squared coefficient of the inter-decision time in the equivalent base-stock inventory system without a processing station.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inter-departure distributions in inventory-queues are not always exponential and can be heavy-tailed.
the inter-departure time in an inventory-queue is not necessarily a renewal process.
